learning: Iteration 0 showed one line-loss excursion per run reaching the 0.06 m floor, with low jitter. Use line_loss_events, first-loss step, and max_error from this race to decide whether the next change is more span or a drivetrain change, and use completion_time to see whether base_speed 1.0 has cost too much time.
notes: Integrated the Builder's 8 cm span with a stronger, better-damped controller (kp 1.0, kd 0.2) and a slower base_speed (1.0) to reduce the single excursion per run seen in iteration 0.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced all 60 trials with every run ending off track after one line-loss event (max_error about 0.061 m, progress 0.11 to 0.16, finish rate 0). Steering oscillation (0.08 to 0.16) and rms_error (about 0.03) are small, so the robot is not jittering or wandering. It is thrown off in one excursion past the 0.06 m floor. The Builder's geometry change widens the outer sensors to x = ±0.04 with inner sensors at ±0.02 and 0, keeping 12 mm footprints and the drivetrain fixed, so this race isolates sensing span. Sensor weights stay at [-2,-1,0,1,2], which keeps the signal scale consistent with the old span. With the wider span, the signal is driven harder by a given lateral offset, so I keep kp near its previous value but raise it slightly to 1.0 so the robot turns back sooner when the tape leaves the outer sensors. I raise kd from 0.1 to 0.2 to damp the faster correction and avoid overshoot, which would otherwise cross the line. I lower base_speed from 1.2 to 1.0 to shorten the time between a loss beginning and the correction, since the excursion is what ends runs. The cost is possibly slower finishes, so if no run finishes, base_speed is the next thing to revisit. ki stays at 0.05 and line_loss stays 'last_direction', which suits losses that happen on bends. Expected result: line_loss_events falls toward zero and max_error drops below 0.06 on the tightest bends. Risk: the wider span may weaken the centroid on gentle bends, which the race's rms_error should show.
